notes: Dev TBox revision. The earlier rule (tropical cyclones turn counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere) was replaced because Olmo and Mistral answered clockwise: two of the four main models do not hold it. The seasons rule is held by every model and stated in Wikipedia's Southern Hemisphere article; the revision moves the southern summer to June to August. The three derived queries name a country, say nothing of its hemisphere, and ask when its summer falls: the model has to supply the hemisphere from what it holds about the country (the bridge, checked before editing) and then apply the edited rule (inheritance, 2 hops); the third asks inside a task (application). Namibia, Mozambique and Madagascar lie wholly south of the equator, and none has its summer months stated by name the way Australia's are (Uruguay was avoided: its Wikipedia article gives summer as December to March). The hemisphere checks are yes/no questions: the earlier "Northern or Southern" form was answered Southern for Bangladesh by all four models. Near unrelated keeps the relation and changes the hemisphere (winter in the Northern Hemisphere): a method that spreads the edit to the other hemisphere would change it. The relation has_summer_in is new (staging/geography.RELATIONS.md; the cyclone relation rotates is no longer used). Further infini-gram counts were not taken: ig_count.py reported "blocked" on 2026-11-12 and Wikipedia search answered HTTP 429, so no more requests were made.
